headline: Launch an AI‑agent platform that automates multi‑step business workflows and showcase it as your startup MVP.
why_now: AI agents are exploding: GitHub activity (96) and growth (94) prove massive developer interest, while Hugging Face (92) and news mentions (88) signal rapid adoption. Employers are already hunting talent (job demand 85) and investors are watching the surge, making this the perfect moment to build a market‑ready demo.
study: 1. Master the fundamentals of LangChain/AutoGPT and tool‑calling APIs (official docs + 2‑hour tutorial).
2. Deep‑dive into prompt engineering for planning and memory management (read "Prompt Engineering for Agents" and run 3 notebook experiments).
3. Implement a simple agent that schedules meetings via Google Calendar API (follow a step‑by‑step guide on GitHub).
4. Explore retrieval‑augmented generation with Hugging Face models to give the agent contextual knowledge (run a mini‑project using Haystack).
5. Study production best practices: containerization, logging, and security for external API calls.

build.title: Workflow‑Wizard: an AI‑agent that automates end‑to‑end sales onboarding
build.description: The agent ingests a new lead’s data, drafts a personalized outreach email, books a discovery call via Calendly, updates the CRM, and generates a follow‑up summary. It demonstrates planning, tool use, and multi‑step execution—exactly what investors look for in a SaaS AI startup.
deliverables: GitHub repo with clean README and CI pipeline
Live demo hosted on Render or Railway

publish: 1. Publish a concise LinkedIn carousel explaining the problem, architecture, and results; tag @LangChain, @OpenAI, and relevant startup incubators.
2. Submit a detailed post to the AI Agents subreddit and Hacker News "Show HN" with a link to the demo.
3. Release a short blog on Medium (or dev.to) that includes code snippets and lessons learned; cross‑post to the Hugging Face Spaces community.
4. Reach out directly to 5 early‑stage VCs or accelerator programs with a personalized email and the pitch video.
risks: API cost overruns if the agent makes many external calls; mitigate with usage caps and mock services during dev.
Prompt brittleness—agents can hallucinate or fail on edge cases; need robust validation and fallback logic.
Market saturation: many agents exist, so differentiation must come from a clear niche (sales onboarding) and polished UX.
confidence: Given the high signal scores across development activity, community buzz, and market demand, this recommendation is very solid for a startup‑focused AI engineer.
